## Introduction

`BayesianEFA` fits Bayesian Exploratory Factor Analysis models with Stan.

- **Unconstrained estimation**: the loading matrix is left free, with no fixed
  parameters or arbitrary identification constraints.
- **Rotational indeterminacy solved**: the draws are aligned with Varimax and
  the Efficient Rotation-Sign-Permutation (E-RSP) algorithm, so the posterior
  of every loading is interpretable.
- **Bayesian fit measures**: the Bayesian SEM fit indices of
  Garnier-Villarreal & Jorgensen (2020) and PSIS-LOO.
- **Full posterior inference**: complete distributions for the loadings, the
  factor scores, the fit measures and the reliability coefficients.
- **FIML for missing data**: incomplete data sets use every observed value.
- **No Heywood cases**: the unit-vector prior keeps every communality below 1.

## Stan backends

`BayesianEFA` writes the Stan program of each model itself and runs it with
one of four interfaces to Stan, all optional:

- **stanli** interprets Stan programs, so it needs no C++ compiler and starts
  at once. It is the default when it is installed:

  ```r
  install.packages("stanli", repos = c("https://seantalts.r-universe.dev",
                                       getOption("repos")))
  stanli::stanli_install()
  ```

- **cmdstanr**, **stanr** and **rstan** compile each program the first time it
  is needed (half a minute to a minute) and keep it in a cache, so later
  sessions start at once. `befa_compile_models()` compiles every program in
  advance, and `befa_clear_cache()` removes them.

With `backend = "auto"` (the default), `befa()` uses the first one installed
among stanli, cmdstanr, stanr and rstan; `backend = "cmdstanr"`, for instance,
chooses one.

## Fitting a model

The following call fits a three-factor model to the Holzinger and Swineford
(1939) data, aligns the draws, and computes the fit indices, the omega
coefficients and, on request, the factor scores:


``` r
library(BayesianEFA)
#> 
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>  BayesianEFA (v0.1.0.9000): Bayesian Exploratory Factor Analysis
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

befa_fit <- befa(
  data = HS_data,        # one row per person, one column per item
  n_factors = 3,         # number of latent factors
  factor_scores = TRUE,  # also draw the factor scores
  seed = 17              # for reproducible results
)
#> BayesianEFA: using the stanli backend.
#> ── Bayesian exploratory factor analysis ────────────────────────────────────────────────── stanli ──
#> ℹ 4 chains of 1000 draws after 1000 warmup iterations, 4 at a time.
#> ✔ Sampled 4 chains in 2.6s.
#> ✔ No divergent transitions.
#> ✔ No transition reached the maximum tree depth (15).
#> ✔ Largest R-hat 1.003, below 1.01.
#> ✔ Smallest effective sample size 2169, above 400.
#> ℹ Drawing the factor scores.
#> ℹ Computing the fit indices and the null model.
```

By default, `befa()` fits the correlation matrix (`model = "cor"`) with the
unit-vector prior on the loadings, and runs four chains of 1000 warmup and
1000 kept iterations of NUTS. After sampling it checks the convergence of the
parameters it returns: the aligned loadings, the uniquenesses and the
communalities.

## Model summary

`summary()` prints tables inspired by the `psych` package. The factors are
ordered by the variance they explain, and the items, listed by their names,
are grouped by the factor of their largest loading (`sort = FALSE` keeps their
original order; long names are shortened to keep the width of the table).
`cutoff` hides the loadings below a threshold, and `signif_stars` marks those
whose 95% credible interval excludes zero. The second table gives the variance
each factor explains:


``` r
summary(befa_fit, cutoff = 0.3, signif_stars = TRUE)
```

## Posterior draws

The fit holds the draws of the final parameters in the metric of the model:
`Lambda_std`, `Psi_std` and `h2` for the correlation model.
`extract_posterior_draws()` returns them in any format of the `posterior`
package, and `posterior_summaries()` summarises them with their convergence
diagnostics:


``` r
draws <- extract_posterior_draws(befa_fit, pars = "Lambda_std")

hist(draws[, "Lambda_std[4,1]"],
  breaks = 50,
  col = "#2780e3",
  border = "white",
  main = "Posterior of Lambda_std[4,1]",
  xlab = "Value"
)
```

![plot of chunk draws](figures/getting-started-draws-1.png)

``` r

posterior_summaries(befa_fit, pars = "h2")
```

## Fit measures, reliability and factor scores

The fit indices and the omega coefficients are part of the fit, and their
functions return them with every draw:



## How many factors?

Several values of `n_factors` fit one model per value, with the same settings
and seed. The saturated and null models are estimated once, and the models are
compared with `befa_compare()`:


``` r
fits <- befa(HS_data, n_factors = 1:3, seed = 17, verbose = FALSE)
summary(fits)
#> 
#> Bayesian EFA with 1, 2, 3 factors
#> Data model: cor; prior: unit_vector; N = 301; rotation: varimax; MCMC with
#> stanli. 
#> 
#> Table 1. Overview of the Models
```

The overview has one row per model, followed by the comparison tables and, so
that the output stays short, the loadings of the model with the highest ELPD.
Showing a model is not selecting it: the note says which simpler models predict
about as well, and `summary(fits, show = 2)` or `summary(fits, show = "all")`
shows others. Each fit is a usual `befa` object (`fits$nf2`). To also compare
the model evidence, add
`compare_criteria = c("fit", "loo", "ic", "evidence")` to the call.

## Other models

- `model = "cov"` fits the covariance matrix and `model = "raw"` also the item
  means. Their draws are in the units of the items;
  `extract_posterior_draws(fit, metric = "std")` returns the standardized
  solution.
- `lambda_prior = "normal"` places normal priors on the loadings of the
  covariance and raw models.
- `missing = "FIML"` uses every observed value of incomplete data.
- Summary statistics replace the data:
  `befa(sample_nobs = 301, sample_cor = cor(HS_data), n_factors = 3)`.
- `method = "pathfinder"` and `method = "advi"` approximate the posterior in
  seconds. `befa()` reports the Pareto k of the approximation, and warns when
  it is above 0.7.
- `befa_compare(two = fit2, three = fit3)` compares fits to the same data
  with different numbers of factors: the fit indices, PSIS-LOO with stacking
  and pseudo-BMA+ weights, the information criteria with Akaike weights, and
  the model evidence from bridge sampling (`befa_bridge_sampler()`) with
  posterior model probabilities, each table ordered from the best model.

- Holzinger, K. J., & Swineford, F. A. (1939). *A Study of Factor Analysis: The Stability of a Bi-Factor Solution.* Supplementary Educational Monograph 48. Chicago: University of Chicago Press.
- McDonald, R. P. (1999). *Test Theory: A Unified Treatment*. Lawrence Erlbaum Associates.
- Rey-Sáez, R., Franco-Martínez, A., Revuelta, J., & Vadillo, M. A. (2026). A unified framework for psychometrics in experimental psychology: The standardized generalized hierarchical factor model. *Psychological Methods*. Advance online publication. <https://doi.org/10.1037/met0000846>
- Rey-Sáez, R., & Revuelta, J. (2026). An efficient rotation-sign-permutation algorithm to solve rotational indeterminacy in Bayesian exploratory factor analysis. *Bayesian Analysis*. Advance publication. <https://doi.org/10.1214/26-BA1611>
